newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Coffee called $100 higher, may do $50 up.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Coffee called $100 higher, may do $50 up.

text.p: JULY Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
LIFFE coffee futures were called $100 a tonne higher on numbers based on New York's surge on Wednesday, but traders said the market could be content with $50-$60 higher.
Chart-wise, July futures are likely to clear the immediate $1,650 hurdle but could struggle to vault above a stiff barrier at $1,700
Adrian Haylor, a technical analyst at Sucden, said July looked sheltered above the immediate support at $1,600.
"I think the resistance we will be looking out today is about $1,700, so expect to move back up to those sort of level," he said.
Beyond that, there is still an uptrend in place which is still holding.
"That's reasonable friendly but we have been trading in a range for one-and-a-half months," Haylor said.
July will also have to fill a chart gap at between $1,705 and $1,730, the high on April 21 and the low on March 12 respectively.
A break above those levels could pave the way for the next assault at $1,820, the last high on March 5.
"Perhaps this move in the U.S. will enable the robusta market to break out to the upside. For the time being, we are stuck in a range," Haylor added.
New York arabica futures burst higher on Wednesday, with many contracts hitting new life-of-contract highs, as continued supply worries sparked a wave of speculative buying.

The rally was led by the spot May contract, which exploded to a new contract high of 240.00 cents per lb, before settling up a hefty 12.65 cents, to 239.05, its highest level on a continuous monthly basis since March 1, 1986.
Benchmark July surged 11.45 cents per lb -- or nearly six percent -- to close at 210.40 cents, after ranging between a new lifetime high of 212.00 and 200.40 cents.
Supplies of coffee certified for delivery against the exchange have dwindled steadily from a build up of more than 83,000 60-kg bags three weeks ago.
Unlike in arabicas, nearby supplies of robustas are ample, judging by the large discount of May futures against July.
London's May enters the month-long tender period on Thursday. Traders said there is a large amount of coffee waiting to be tendered.
Trading in London will be restricted by a public holiday in many European countries. --Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
